Dudley's population increased by around 10,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 320,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Dudley increased by 3.4%, from just over 312,900 in 2011 to around 323,500 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Dudley was home to around 23.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 22.8 in 2011. This area was among the top 20% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Dudley than across the West Midlands

Median age stable in Dudley

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 41 years in Dudley between the last two censuses.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 6,800 (an increase of 11.9%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 7,700 (11.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

More lone parents

Dudley saw the West Midlands' second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of lone-parent households (from 10.6% in 2011 to 12.1% in 2021).

Across the region, only Walsall saw a greater rise in the percentage of lone-parent households (from 12.0% to 14.0%).

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of lone-parent households increased from 11.3% to 11.8%, while the percentage in nearby Sandwell increased from 13.5% to 14.9%.

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Dudley increased by 1.5 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Dudley saw the West Midlands' largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (from 31.2% in 2011 to 35.9% in 2021).

Walsall saw the West Midlands' next largest increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership (from 32.9% in 2011 to 37.5% in 2021).

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a rise in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership, as the regional percentage grew from 33.7% to 37.1%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Dudley increased by 4.7 percentage points

Rise in private renting

In 2021, 13.8% of Dudley households rented privately. This figure increased from 9.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in five households (19.0%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 19.8% in 2011. The percentage of Dudley households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 68.8% to 66.4%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Dudley (4.6 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (3.9 percentage points, from 14.0% to 17.9%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Dudley increased by 4.6 percentage points

Unpaid care in Dudley

In 2021, 5.0% of Dudley residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.0% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.8% in 2011. The proportion of Dudley residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 3.3% to 3.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Dudley (3.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Dudley decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Dudley

In 2021, 8.4% of Dudley residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 6.1% in 2011. The 2.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 10.8% to 13.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 84.9% of people in Dudley identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.0% in 2011), while 2.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.8% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.5% in 2011 to 2.5% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 8.4% of usual residents in Dudley identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Dudley

In 2021, 36.0% of Dudley residents reported having "No religion", up from 22.0% in 2011. The rise of 14.0 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Dudley. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.3% of people in Dudley described themselves as Christian (down from 65.3%), while 6.2% described themselves as Muslim (up from 4.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 36.0% of usual residents in Dudley reported having "No religion"

National identity in Dudley

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in nearby Sandwell (4.9 percentage points) than in Dudley (1.7 percentage points).

In Dudley, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 2.3% in 2011 to 4.1% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Sandwell increased from 8.8% to 13.8%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Dudley increased from 0.3% to 0.8%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 14.1% to 54.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Dudley increased by 1.7 percentage points

Dudley residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 294,400 Dudley residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.0% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 292,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.4% of Dudley's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with around 5,300 Dudley residents reporting this country of birth (1.7%). This figure was up from just under 4,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.3% of the population of Dudley.

The number of Dudley residents born in India rose from around 2,300 in 2011 (0.7% of the local population) to around 2,900 in 2021 (0.9%).

In 2021, 91.0% of Dudley residents reported their country of birth as England

Disability in Dudley

The increase in the age-standardised proportion of non-disabled residents was greater in nearby Sandwell (4.4 percentage points) than in Dudley (1.8 percentage points).

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In Dudley, the proportion of non-disabled residents increased from 79.0% in 2011 to 80.8% in 2021. During the same period, the proportion in nearby Sandwell increased from 75.6% to 80.0%.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Dudley fell from 10.2% to 8.3%, while the percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little increased from 10.8% to 10.9%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of non-disabled residents in Dudley increased by 1.8 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Dudley residents aged 16 years and over, 53.9% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 54.6% in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 30 people (3.3%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.8% in 2011. The percentage of retired Dudley residents remained at 24.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater across the West Midlands (1.1 percentage points, from 54.4% to 53.3%) than in Dudley (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Dudley decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Working hours in Dudley

In 2021, 9.1% of Dudley residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was the same in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 11 people (9.2%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 10.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 59.3% to 61.2%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 9.6% to 9.9% across the West Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Dudley decreased by 0.1 percentage points

Health in Dudley

In 2021, 43.6% of Dudley residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 41.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.2% to 35.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Dudley residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.3% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.3% to 4.7%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Dudley increased by 2.3 percentage points
